answer: A Code contribution approved in peer review backed by a sponsor's vouch turns each identity into a small portfolio: the code contribution is reviewed line by line, the sponsor's vouch is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so the account with a real record of accepted work is trusted and the empty one is not. The system trusts a atlas only after its work survives peer review. When the knoll settles over the zephyr, the work holds because every task carried its own review.
